title: Headless E-Commerce Backend on Cloudflare Workers
context: We need to design a high-performance, cost-effective, and low-latency headless backend for an e-commerce application. The backend must handle real-time inventory management, integration with Stripe (payments), and FedEx/USPS (shipping calculations). It must run entirely in a serverless environment on Cloudflare Workers.

options_considered.option: Option A: Monolithic Worker with Hono and Cloudflare D1
pros: Simple implementation and deployment within a single project.
Transactional safety inside D1 database for inventory checks.
cons: Risk of V8 isolate bundle size limits if bloated with external SDKs.
SQLite-backed D1 is localized, may have write locks under heavy loads.

options_considered.option: Option B: Decoupled Workers with Durable Objects for Inventory
pros: Strong consistency and single-threaded execution for inventory prevents race conditions entirely.
Clear boundary separation between catalog, checkout, and order domains.
cons: Higher operational costs (Durable Objects require paid Cloudflare Plan).
Increased architecture complexity with inter-worker bindings.

decision: We accept Option A (Monolithic Worker with Hono & D1) for the MVP phase. To resolve inventory race conditions, we will use D1's SQL-level transactional queries (atomic decrements with condition checks) rather than relying on KV cache. Stripe webhooks will trigger order processing, and a Workers Cron Trigger will handle automatic cleanup of unpaid pending orders (timeout at 30 minutes).

positive: Extremely cost-effective running on Cloudflare Free/Pro plans.
Atomic inventory updates via D1 database engine.
negative: Bundle size must be carefully monitored (must not exceed 1MB uncompressed).
Cron scheduler executes at 5-minute intervals, meaning some unpaid order cancellations might be delayed up to 34 minutes.

migration_plan: Initialize D1 database migrations for schema setup. Deploy worker with Wrangler env pointing to staging D1 binding. Once verified, bind to production D1 and deploy.
rollback_plan: Execute 'wrangler rollback' to revert to the previous working deployment hash.
